questions.q: 'While we ___(play) cricket, it started to rain.'
questions.a: 'were playing' — background action in progress when the rain interrupted. A wrong answer 'played' flattens both events into one instant — missing the while-pattern entirely.

questions.q: Fix: 'He didn't went to school yesterday.'
questions.a: 'He didn't go' — after 'did', the main verb returns to base form; the past is already carried by 'did'. A wrong answer 'didn't goed' or keeping 'went' shows double-past marking.

questions.q: 'I have decided — I ___ visit Agra this summer.' will or going to?
questions.a: 'am going to' — the plan already exists ('I have decided'). A wrong answer 'will' misses the will/going-to split: will = fresh decisions/predictions, going to = existing plans.

questions.q: Past and future have matching pairs: simple past for finished actions ('She danced yesterday'), past ______ for ongoing past ('She was dancing when I arrived'); simple future = will + base ('She will dance'), and 'going to' for planned future ('She is going to dance tomorrow').

Fill in the blank: The ______-action pattern is the heart: 'While she WAS DANCING, the music STOPPED' — long background action (continuous) cut by a short event (simple past).
What is Past and future have matching pairs? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Past and future have matching pairs: simple past for finished actions ('She danced yesterday'), past continuous for ongoing past ('She was dancing when I arrived'); simple future = will + base ('She will dance'), and 'going to' for planned future ('She is going to dance tomorrow').

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Past and future have matching pairs?
questions.a: Students learn irregular pasts as lists without patterns, write 'didn't went' (double past — after 'did' the verb returns to base form), and use will/going-to interchangeably.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student forms and chooses between simple past and past continuous (the interrupted-action pattern), and between will and going-to for predictions vs plans.
